reasons.D: Two pale antlers spreading past the head over broad, dark smoke-cured hide give the clearest barbarian outline of the six from the ARPG camera, and nothing in the existing families has horns.
reasons.A: A pale beast-skull helm with horns over dark hide and a wolf-fur mantle reads as 'trophy-taker' at a glance; the skull is the strongest single read on the sheet.
reasons.E: The asymmetric skull pauldron with one arm bare makes a lopsided outline no other family has, which is exactly the half-armoured fury in the brief.

fixes.D: The grey shoulder plates and brow strip push it toward the iron family's grey at the ARPG camera; warm them toward hide or bone so the horns stay the only bright line.
fixes.A: The arms read as bare body; check on real avatars that skin, not the dummy's blue, carries the set, and consider a hide bracer so the arm isn't empty.
fixes.E: Its bare left arm and the skull pauldron are the idea; the chest under them is plain dark hide and could carry a fur edge or a strap of bone.

notes: 6 of 6 survived, all within the budget (59 to 63 of 64), with no turn-cap failures at 70 turns. Every set used near-black smoke-cured hide; the swarm converged on dark hide plus pale bone or fur as the barbarian family read, which is coherent, but a future brief could ask for a warmer or painted alternative. Bare arms show the preview dummy's blue: a Studio check on real avatars matters more here than for other families.
